title: Why the DeLisa succeeded and Saunders as community figure
summary: A friendly place with bouncers who protected customers; he stayed connected through NAACP, Urban League and social club work.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: What do you think the -- perhaps you already said it, why that club was so successful? Was it based on personalities involved? Your band and the show --

Right, it was a club that you'd come in, and if you come in a stranger, you would go out knowing people and then having friends. And then, the whole personnel of the club, if you'd come back again, you were like coming to a place where you knew practically everybody.

Then they had these big bouncers, man, they had a guy there about six-six, weighing about 270. And he wouldn't let nothing happen to nobody. So that was one of the main things. People felt free, they felt free -- see, when you're

drinking, you have a fear of going too far, and then getting your head bashed in. But it wasn't like that. Even the guy out in front, the doorman, he would look out for you, see that you got into your car and all that type of thing.
But there wasn't too much going on.
And it was easy to get there, even if you didn't have a car. By the El.

Right, right. It was by the State Street -- the transportation there, elevated. I used to walk across the -- I mean, walk from my house. I used to live at 55th and King Drive, and I would walk over every night, and never no trouble or nothing. Every once in a while one of the sporting girls who was new on the block, she would whistle at me, and they'd say, 'don't pay him no mind, that's Red.'
Well, you became a community figure, too, didn't you?

Right, right, right, see, so -- and through all of the different organizations and things that I played for and all of that. NAACP, the Urban League and all of these things. And then all the social clubs I was telling you about, I just kept that communication going.
Yeah, everything stems from the Delisa.
